$comment: What does not carry over between Svelte, React and Vue, and the explicit contract that replaces it. `xgen check` fails when a marker shows up in generated code of its runtime.

features.feature: setContext / getContext: values handed down the tree without props
features.replacement: An explicit port. The URL is a UrlPort object created by the app and passed to the screen as the `url` prop (a rune store in Svelte, useSyncExternalStore in React); nothing is read from context.
One-way `value` plus an event prop (`oninput` / `onChange`): the parent owns the state and the URL is the state.
Not used. Behaviour lives in portable TypeScript (xgen/runtimes/core/assets/app) and in event props.
The same explicit `url` prop as in Svelte.

features.feature: {@html}: an HTML string rendered as markup
features.replacement: Not used. Markup is built from kit primitives by the emitter; text comes from content as text (rules 02 and 06, group rules).

features.feature: dangerouslySetInnerHTML: an HTML string rendered as markup
features.replacement: Not used. Markup is built from kit primitives by the emitter; text comes from content as text (rules 02 and 06, group rules).

features.feature: v-html: an HTML string rendered as markup
features.replacement: Not used. Markup is built from kit primitives by the emitter; text comes from content as text (rules 02 and 06, group rules).

features.feature: v-model: two-way binding of a prop
features.replacement: One-way `:value` plus an event prop (`@input`), as in Svelte and React: the parent owns the state and the URL is the state.

features.feature: Slot with arguments: a Svelte snippet (`{#snippet footer(plan)}`) versus a React render function (`footer={(plan) => ...}`)
features.replacement: The organism spec declares slots with typed arguments (slots[].args). Each emitter prints its own form; the screen spec fills the slot with the same nodes, and the argument names are part of the contract.

features.feature: Children: a Svelte Snippet versus React ReactNode, and `asChild` (React only)
features.replacement: Bricks declare a `children` slot. `asChild` is a React-only option of the brick and is listed in its runtimeNotes; screens never use it.
